description: The card filter blank on the SPACES route while the account filter is valid: the operator typed nothing at all into CARDSID, 'Card number not provided' therefore reaches the screen because the account edit left the single message slot free, and the cursor EVALUATE takes its second arm on the second of that arm's two conditions. 2200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS sets INPUT-OK, FLG-CARDFILTER-ISVALID and FLG-ACCTFILTER-ISVALID at :610-612, then normalises: ACCTSIDI is neither '*' nor SPACES at :615-616 so :619 moves the eleven typed characters into CC-ACCT-ID, while CARDSIDI is sixteen spaces so :622-623 matches on its SPACES disjunct and :624 moves LOW-VALUES into CC-CARD-NUM. 2210-EDIT-ACCOUNT then SUCCEEDS, which is the whole point of the case: it sets FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK at :648, fails the not-supplied test at :651-653 on all three disjuncts - not LOW-VALUES, not SPACES, and CC-ACCT-ID-N is 27 rather than ZEROS - fails IS NOT NUMERIC at :665, and so runs the ELSE at :675-677, moving CC-ACCT-ID into CDEMO-ACCT-ID and setting FLG-ACCTFILTER-ISVALID. It writes no message, so WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF still holds when 2220-EDIT-CARD runs. 2220 sets FLG-CARDFILTER-NOT-OK at :688, matches the not-supplied test at :691-693 on its LOW-VALUES disjunct, sets INPUT-ERROR and FLG-CARDFILTER-BLANK, and this time IF WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF at :696 PASSES - so :697 sets WS-PROMPT-FOR-CARD, and the twenty-four characters of 'Card number not provided' reach WS-RETURN-MSG PIC X(75) and then ERRMSGO PIC X(80) through :494, twenty-four significant characters followed by fifty-six spaces. That guard is the assertion this case exists for, and it is the exact mirror of case06: there the account edit had already claimed the single message slot, so the identical SET was skipped and the flag survived alone. The cross-field edit at :637-640 needs FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK AND FLG-CARDFILTER-BLANK, and the account flag is ISVALID, so NO-SEARCH-CRITERIA-RECEIVED is never set: 'No input received' must not appear anywhere here, and neither must 'Account number not provided'. Those three texts are mutually exclusive by ordering alone, and the pair of cases is what makes the ordering provable (gate G30). Note also the asymmetry the two edits carry, preserved rather than tidied (practice B5): :676 moves CC-ACCT-ID, the alphanumeric X(11) view, whereas :717 moves CC-CARD-NUM-N, the numeric 9(16) REDEFINES. Both reach a numeric receiver and the difference changes nothing for a valid value, so it is kept because the source says it. INPUT-ERROR at :360 then sends the map and goes to COMMON-RETURN, so 9000-READ-DATA is never reached: a perfectly valid account buys nothing once the card field is empty, no CARDDAT read is issued at either the base-key or the alternate-key entry point - 9150-GETCARD-BYACCT is never performed from anywhere and stays dead code (gate G45, practice B5) - and the three seeded rows are asserted byte for byte exactly as seeded, with an empty write channel as the other half of that statement. 1200-SETUP-SCREEN-VARS then paints asymmetrically: EIBCALEN is 172, so the ELSE arm runs; CDEMO-ACCT-ID is now 27 and therefore non-zero, so :465 echoes CC-ACCT-ID into ACCTSIDO as '00000000027', while CDEMO-CARD-NUM was zeroed at :700 so :471 leaves CARDSIDO at LOW-VALUES; FOUND-CARDS-FOR-ACCOUNT is false because nothing was read, so CRDNAMEO, CRDSTCDO, EXPMONO and EXPYEARO stay as MOVE LOW-VALUES TO CCRDSLAO left them at :428 - binary zero, not spaces; and WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE at :490 still holds, so WS-PROMPT-FOR-INPUT puts the thirty-six-character 'Please enter Account and Card Number' into INFOMSGO PIC X(40). 1300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS is where this case earns its place. The turn does not arrive from the card list - CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET is 'COCRDSL' and CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM is 'COCRDSLC', so the conjunction at :505-506 is false - which sends both ACCTSIDA and CARDSIDA of the input group to DFHBMFSE and leaves the DFHDFCOL at :528-529 unwritten. The cursor EVALUATE at :515-524 is ordered, and arm one is false on both of its conditions because the account flag is ISVALID, so arm two wins on its second condition, FLG-CARDFILTER-BLANK: :520 moves -1 into CARDSIDL and ACCTSIDL is never touched. Arm one is not even a candidate on this path, and the arm-two condition driven is FLG-CARDFILTER-BLANK rather than FLG-CARDFILTER-NOT-OK - a distinction worth stating, because the arm is reachable both ways and the two conditions colour the field through different guards further down. The blankness itself arrives through the SPACES disjunct of :622-623, which is the disjunct a genuinely untyped field takes, rather than through the '*' marker a previous turn may have left in the same field. The colour guards then fire exactly once between them: :533 is false, :537 is false because the card flag is BLANK and not NOT-OK - the same one-byte field carries '0' for NOT-OK, '1' for ISVALID and a space for BLANK, and SET FLG-CARDFILTER-BLANK replaced the NOT-OK :688 had set - :541 is false, and only :547-551 runs, moving '*' into CARDSIDO and DFHRED into CARDSIDC. So the screen leaves with ACCTSIDO showing '00000000027' with no asterisk and no red, and CARDSIDO showing an asterisk with DFHRED beside it, and that one-sided outcome is the assertion. MOVE '*' space-fills its X(16) receiver rather than leaving the LOW-VALUES behind, because a one-character literal moved to an alphanumeric item pads on the right; ACCTSIDC is reported DFHDFCOL because 0x00 is that mnemonic on the colour plane and nothing ever wrote to it. COCRDSLC copies no CSSETATY - only COACTUPC does - and re-implements the highlight inline with the BLANK path gated on CDEMO-PGM-REENTER and the NOT-OK path ungated, so this case owns the gated blank side of gate G38 while the NOT-OK cases own the ungated one; flattening the two would silently stop colouring a rejected filter on first entry. INFOMSGC is DFHNEUTR from :556 because 1200 has already filled WS-INFO-MSG. 1400-SEND-SCREEN then moves LIT-THISMAPSET, which is PIC X(8) VALUE 'COCRDSL ', into CCARD-NEXT-MAPSET PIC X(7) - a PIC X receiver truncates on the right, so the surviving mapset is 'COCRDSL' - names CCRDSLA as the map, and sets CDEMO-PGM-REENTER, so the returned context is 1 again; :588 had already named COCRDSLC as CCARD-NEXT-PROG. COMMON-RETURN lays the 160-byte CARDDEMO-COMMAREA and the twelve-byte WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA into WS-COMMAREA and issues EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID('CCDL'), so every byte of conversation state travels in the payload and nothing is retained on the server (gate G37, rule R6). The two commarea transitions are deliberately observable: the account arrives as eleven zeros and leaves as 00000000027, which is :676 taking effect, and the card arrives as 0683586198171516 and leaves as sixteen zeros, which is :700. The clock is pinned to 2022-07-19T23:16:00, so CURDATEO and CURTIMEO are the literals 07/19/22 and 23:16:00 rather than today (practice B7). Gates G32, G35 and G39 have no site here: every GO TO in this program is a forward early exit or the shared COMMON-RETURN, so there is no backward loop to restructure; there is no CALL 'CEE3ABD' anywhere in COCRDSLC, whose abend path is the CICS-native HANDLE ABEND at :250-252 into ABEND ABCODE('9999'); and COCRDSL declares no PAGENO and no EXPDAY. Rule R4 likewise has no site - COCRDSLC holds no PIC 9(n)V(n) monetary field, so gates G22 to G28 have no call site on this path. The class is named CardSelectController because the migration plan names it so, while the source Function header, README.md:213-231 and CARDDEMO.CSD:220 DESCRIPTION(VIEW CARD DETAIL) all describe a card detail view - honoured verbatim per rule R1 and documented rather than corrected per practice B4, register AAP 0.8.4. No user rules govern this repository - review_rules returns exactly 'No user rules provided' - so the binding constraints on this fixture are the enterprise practices B1, B3, B4, B5, B7, B8, B11 and B12 rather than any project rule. Every expected value here was derived by structured reading of app/cbl/COCRDSLC.cbl against the app/cpy-bms/COCRDSL.CPY xxxI and xxxO PICTURE clauses, the app/cpy/CVACT02Y.cpy record layout, the app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy title literals whose line 21 is commented out and line 22 active, app/bms/COCRDSL.bms and the real US-ASCII fixture whose row at index 1 genuinely carries account 00000000027 and card 0683586198171516; none of it was captured from a running COBOL program, because this environment cannot run one - eight blockers are recorded in AAP 0.7.6 and the substitution is escalated as risk R-A (practice B12).
